prerequisites: It is recommended to have taken the course Foreign Language I, which, starting from a B1 level of English, prepares students to adequately access the current course, as the objective is to reach the officially required technical B2 level.

It is essential to start the course with a B1+ level of English in both comprehension and oral and written communication, as students who do not have the required level will have serious problems passing the course.

learning_outcomes.text: Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Demonstrate an entrepreneurial attitude in the design, development and execution of solutions that represent a novelty or advance in the field of the discipline.
Function effectively in a team whose members together provide leadership and create a collaborative and inclusive environment in the organization and coordination of work.
Proactively collaborate in the development of work, setting goals and meeting objectives.
Structure discourse to facilitate the understanding of the objectives, actions and/or results of one's own work.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in various situations and/or before diverse audiences.

teaching_methods: Team projects (problem-solving through planning, design, execution)
Individual and group preparation of essays
Student study (readings, exam preparation, exercise elaboration, class preparation)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment - Simulation activities in small groups or pairs
Continuous assessment - Programmed review tests of class content

assessment_rules: The overall grade for the first call is derived from continuous assessment (50%) and a final exam (50%). Continuous assessment scores are only considered if a minimum of 2 out of 5 (40%) is obtained in the final exam (combined written and oral parts). To be eligible for the oral exam, a minimum score of 1 must be achieved in the combined Writing and Listening sections of the written exam. For the second call, students have three options: take a 100% final exam, combine a 50% final exam with their first-call continuous assessment score, or combine a 50% final exam with a partial retake of continuous assessment components.
